newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - May 27.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Following a warning from BHP executive John Prescott that the company's final-quarter profit would be well below market expectations, the sharemarket reacted by wiping 40 cents from the Big Australian's share price - a loss of A$800 million in market capitalisation. Most analysts cut their forecasts for BHP's 1996-97 profit by more than A$100 million to less than A$1.4 billion. Page 1.

In a move following an investigation by the Australian Securities Commission into suspicious trading in TNT Ltd call options in September last year, Macquarie Bank senior executive Simon Hannes appeared in Sydney's St James Local Court yesterday charged wth one count of insider trading in TNT securities. Page 1.

According to the Foodweek market share survey, independent grocery stores are continuing to lose ground, while supermarket giants Coles Myer Ltd and Woolworths Ltd have lifted their share of the A$40 billion market to more than two-thirds. The survey revealed Woolworths lifted its share of supermarket sales by 0.3 per cent to 35.1 per cent, while Coles' share increased by 1.6 per cent to 27.9 per cent of sales. Page 23.

It is understood that the independent directors of Coal & Allied Industries Ltd will be asked tomorrow to adopt proposals and to merge the board's management and administration with another of RTZ-CRA's Hunter Valley coal subsidiaries, Novacoal Pty Ltd, saving the cost of two head offices for two poorly performing firms. Page 23.

In a move which will create Australia's largest food service group, with annual sales of A$600 million, Davids Ltd's Lewis Foodservice and Rick Smith's Glacier Holdings Australia Pty Ltd, trading as PFD Food Services, announced an alliance yesterday,with Glacier Holdings taking a 40 per cent stake in the merged entity. Page 23.

An Feng Steel Co president A.H. Chu said yesterday his company and proposed merger partner Kingstream Resources NL, led by Perth businessman Ken Court, will press ahead with a A$500 million capital raising following yesterday's endorsement of the merger by independent expert Grant Samuel. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Just four weeks before BHP announces its 1997 annual result, chief executive John Prescott has warned the market the company's "flat" performance is likely to continue through the first half of next year. The announcement saw analysts downgrading their prfit forecasts for Australia's biggest company, wiping almost A$800 million off its market value yesterday. Page 19.

Productivity Commission chairman Bill Scales announced yesterday the Commission's report on car tariffs, due to be presented to Federal Treasurer Peter Costello yesterday, has been delayed until "some time this week" after Mitsubishi Motors, the New South Wales Government and the South Australian Labor Party lodged last-minute submissions. Page 19.

Following a six-month inquiry by the Australian Securities Commission, top Macquarie Bank Ltd executive Simon Gautier Hannes has been charged with insider trading in TNT options using the alias M Booth. The ASC alleges Hannes bought five million A$2 call ptions over TNT shares, knowing a bid for the transport giant was in the offing. Page 19.

According to a study released yesterday by the Australian Gas Association at its industry forum in Canberra, huge growth in demand for gas in domestic and global markets will fuel a A$19 billion investment boom in the industry to 2005. The study indicates new multi-billion-dollar pipeline and field investments will be required to meet the anticipated strong demand. Page 21.

Speaking at the Foodweek conference in Sydney yesterday, Woolworths Ltd managing director Reg Clairs told industry players Woolworths had moved into wholesaling, prepared foods, exports and petrol retailing because it saw itself as a food distribution busness, rather than simply a supermarket business. Clairs urged retailers and suppliers to look beyond the supermarket business for growth. Page 21.

Federal Resources Minister Warwick Parer announced yesterday CRA Ltd managing director Leigh Clifford will head the Government's Gas Reform and Implementation Group to kick-start the stalled gas reform process, thereby creating a national gas market free of State barriers. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

BHP hosed down profit expectations yesterday, blaming the cost of its restructuring and difficult trading conditions. Analysts cut their forecasts of about A$360 million by up to A$100 million for BHP's fourth quarter. BHP revealed its flat profit performance would extend into its 1997-98 May financial year. Page 25.

Rupert Murdoch was briefed by Foxtel management on a flying visit to Sydney yesterday, coinciding with attempts by Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting to fast-track a restructuring of the pay TV industry. News Ltd has been holding talks with PBL on a range of subjects including the immediate future of Australis. Industry experts believe Australis will struggle to survive this year. Page 25.

Former Macquarie Bank executive Simon Hannes was charged with insider training yesterday, in relation to 5,000 TNT options contracts bought in the name of M. Booth two weeks before a friendly takeover bid for TNT in 1996. He allegedly used his high-level access to enter the bank's corporate advisory section at least six times, late at night while on leave. Page 25.

Stockbroking analysts said yesterday the furore over the major banks' decision not to pass on the full reduction in official interest rates would harm Westpac's chances of approval for its A$1.4 billion takeover of Bank of Melbourne . National Australia Bank's hopes of convincing the Federal Government to lift the "four pillars" policy, restricting it from buying another major, are also likely to be harmed. Page 27.

New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan signalled a strong openness to heavy foreign investment in the power industry yesterday. He named Pacific Power as the only power company requiring majority Australian ownership under the proposal to sell the State's utilities for up to A$22 billion. Page 27.

Colonial is making tens of thousands of dollars a day in interest from money received for its share offer, revealing it has no intention of mailing out refunds before May 30. Hundreds of thousands of small investors are waiting for hundreds of millions of dollars in refunds after applications for the Colonial share offer were drastically scaled back. Page 27.
THE AGE

BHP shares fell 40 cents to A$18.92? yesterday following a warning from managing director John Prescott that the group's flat profit performance would extend into its 1997-98 May financial year, due largely to the costs of its massive restructuring and dificult trading conditions. Page B1.

In a move which represents a rare attempt by Australian authorities to secure a conviction for insider trading, the Australian Securities Commission yesterday charged upmarket banker Simon Hannes, a former executive of the Macquarie Bank, with insider trading over the deal called "Project Tennis" - last October's A$2 billion takeover of TNT. Page B1.

According to a damning report released yesterday by a parliamentary committee, there is overwhelming evidence of unfair behaviour by big business towards smaller competitors, and due to complaints from retail tenants in shopping complexes across the county, market rents should not be changed for another five years. Page B3.

In an interview following his proposal last week for a A$22 billion power sell-off, New South Wales Treasurer Michael Egan said yesterday there was a strong openness to intensive foreign investment in the industry and Pacific Power was the only power compny in the State that needed to have majority Australian ownership. Page B3.

After receiving the endorsement of independent consultants Grant Samuel yesterday, a merger between Taiwanese steelmaker An Feng Steel and the West Australian-based Kingstream Resources NL to create a A$1 billion integrated steel company could receive shareholder approval as early as next month. Page B3.

According to the Australian Gas Association's Gas Supply and Demand Study 1997, the nation's natural gas industry would need a capital investment of A$14 billion in the years to 2005 - a 40 per cent annual increase over current levels. The study also saidnew pipelines, exploration, and a rise in domestic gas requirements would all increase the need for investment. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
